transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because the doctor doing my insurance physical told me my weight was too low. I mean, they made a bit of a deal about it, but to me, I just look lean. I'm a painter, so I'm up and down ladders and working long days all the time, so it makes sense to me. But yeah, that's why they told me I needed to come see you.
What is your main reason for wanting to stay at your current weight or lose weight?

I guess it's just that... I really don't want it to go up. If I check the scale and it goes up even a little bit—like, maybe after a dinner with a client or if I eat something with bread—I get pretty tense about it. So I just start cutting back the next day to make sure the weight doesn't stick. I just prefer to keep things exactly where they are.
When you look at your body, do you feel that you are overweight or need to lose weight even when other people tell you that you are very thin?

I wouldn't say I look at myself and think I'm massively overweight. But... I do fixate on certain things. Like, when I catch myself in a mirror, or if I'm looking at photos of myself standing next to one of my murals, I basically judge the whole day by whether my stomach and my face look sharp enough. If they don't look lean to me, then yeah, I feel like I need to trim down, regardless of what that insurance doctor or anyone else says.
Have you ever had an episode when you felt unable to control how much you were eating?

No, not really. I don't think I've ever had a time where I felt like I couldn't stop or didn't have control over it. If anything, it's the exact opposite. I always know exactly how much I'm eating, and I keep a pretty tight handle on it.
Has your weight been significantly below what is considered healthy for someone of your height and build?

Well, I guess that's actually why I'm here. I had to get a physical for my insurance, and the doctor there told me my weight was too low. He said it was below what's healthy for my height. I mean, I don't really see it that way. To me, I just look lean. I'm up and down ladders all day, working long hours painting, so it just makes sense that I'd be on the thinner side. But yeah, according to that doctor, it's significantly below where it should be.
Have you ever deliberately made yourself vomit after eating?
No, I've never done that. I don't make myself throw up. Like I said, I just keep a close eye on what I eat to begin with, so I don't feel the need to do anything like that.

Becomes tense when the scale increases even slightly.

Maintains tight control over how much is eaten.
Judges the day based on whether the stomach and face look sufficiently sharp or lean.

Does not recognize the reported low weight as unhealthy and views it as simply being lean.
Denies episodes of feeling unable to control eating.

additional_requirements: Restricting presentation supported by absence of reported binge eating or purging.
